column6: Plain language on every turn: define every term on first use, no analogies, no bare name-drops, no unexpanded acronyms, a phase named with its purpose, and existing terminology only — never an invented term or alias.

column1: non-technical-user
column6: The code overlay for a non-technical owner: every technical name paired with a plain translation the owner learns from, every coding decision framed as the behavior change the owner will see, and never a raw log/diff/output dump in chat.

column1: concise-chat
column6: Objective concise chat: fewest words that carry the message, lead with the decision or result, never restate what a file already says, TLDR bullets on long explanations, and the fixed question format — max 3 at a time, named options with consequences, one recommended.

column1: audio-aware
column6: Use whenever dealing with transcripts — dictated owner input, meeting transcripts, or native harness audio/voice. Ungarbles them: glossary-corrects names (glossary at .rbtv/config/audio/glossary.md, updated same-turn on owner correction), keeps only the speaker's final self-correction, latest version wins on hesitant numbers/dates, flags unknown names instead of assuming, and confirms dates/names in a summary table before any vault write.
